**Finding submitted: deviation (LOL-CAP), Section 15.3 (¶ p0273–p0274).**

- **Cap exists and is mutual** (both the consequential-damages waiver in 15.3(a) and the cap in 15.3(b) run to "either Party"), so mutuality is not the problem.
- **Basis fails the fallback:** 3% of bill-of-materials value of all Products delivered across the whole term is materially below twelve months' — or even six months' — fees for a contract-manufacturing relationship of this volume.
- **No carve-outs:** because the cap covers "total liability ... regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort," MSL's Section 15.1 indemnities (third-party IP infringement, legal non-compliance, warranty support) and its confidentiality obligations all sit inside that low cap with no super-cap — squarely in walk-away territory.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** minimal edit to 15.3(b) only — cap basis becomes the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus one carve-out sentence (indemnities, confidentiality/data security, IP infringement, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud) and confirmation that IBM's payment obligations are not capped damages.
- Per the planner hint, the IBM-drafted Equipment/Program Loan Agreement Section 15, Section 13 disclaimer and the CI Agreement Section 7 disclaimers were reviewed and not flagged, as they operate in our favour.
